diagnosis: WinError 10054 (connection reset by peer) is caused by the Qdrant Cloud server (GCP Australia) closing idle HTTP keep-alive connections after a server-side timeout. The shared httpx connection pool in a single QdrantClient instance holds the stale TCP socket and attempts to reuse it for the next request, causing a ConnectionResetError. This only manifests after enough elapsed time across a 30-case full batch; 10 queries with 3s sleep (diagnostic) completed 10/10 without error.
fix_applied: Option A + Option B combined: (A) A fresh QdrantClient is created before each case in the for-identifier loop and stored via store._client, replacing the old stale client; the old client is closed before the new one is created. (B) _run_case_with_retry wraps each case evaluation with up to 3 retries on transport errors (WinError 10054 / ConnectionResetError / OSError errno 10054), using exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s capped at 30s) and re-swapping the client on retry.
test_details: 14 passed (3 from test_step5_frozen_transport.py + 11 from test_step5_frozen_transport_retry.py), 0 failed. Diagnostic run: 10/10 Qdrant dense queries succeeded with 3s sleep intervals (prefer_grpc=False, HTTP REST, GCP Australia endpoint).
